Taxonomy of NCBI taxids from a local database

Source: R/get_tax.R
get_tax.Rd

Looks up the NCBI taxonomy of taxids in a local SQLite database: no internet, no efetch, thousands of taxids in a few seconds. Returns the minimal table, with one row per distinct taxid, to be joined to the BLAST hits by taxid.

x can be a vector of taxids or any result of parallel_blast() (long or wide) or parallel_blast_hsps(): the taxids are taken from the staxid, k_staxid and Taxids at best columns. Unknown taxids (0, empty, N/A) are dropped.

The database comes with the BLAST databases downloaded by download_blast_db() (taxonomy = TRUE). Without it, get_tax() builds it only when asked (download = TRUE, a taxdump, or a yes in an interactive session), from the NCBI taxdump (about 80 MB, downloaded once, then reused); otherwise it stops and says how. If x is a BLASTr result, the taxdump is the first one the NCBI published after the date of its BLAST database, so the taxonomy matches the database; the database is kept in the BLASTr cache as taxonomy_<database date>.sqlite. With only taxids and no database set, the newest database in the cache is used, or one is built from the current taxdump.

The database has the tables nodes (id, rank, parent) and names (id, name, scientific, type), as built by make_taxonomy_db() (or by taxonomizr::prepareDatabase(), whose file can be used as is). Build it from the NCBI taxdump of the same date as the BLAST database: taxids newer than the taxdump are not found.

Usage

get_tax(
  x,
  taxonomy_db = NULL,
  ranks = tax_ranks_default,
  taxdump = NULL,
  download = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Taxids (character or numeric) or a BLASTr result.

taxonomy_db

Path to the SQLite taxonomy database. NULL uses the option BLASTr.taxonomy_db or the environment variable BLASTR_TAXONOMY_DB; with none set, a database in the BLASTr cache (see below). If the file does not exist, it is built.

ranks

Ranks returned as columns. "domain" is also filled from "superkingdom", its name in taxdumps before 2025.

taxdump

NCBI taxdump used to build a missing database (see make_taxonomy_db()). NULL: the taxdump matching the BLAST database of x (the first monthly NCBI archive after its date), or the current one.

download

Download the NCBI taxdump and build the database when it does not exist. FALSE (default) stops with a message instead (or asks, in an interactive session).

Value

A tibble with one row per taxid: taxid, found (FALSE when the taxid is not in the database), sci_name, rank (rank of the taxid itself), one column per rank in ranks (NA when the lineage has no node of that rank), lineage (all the nodes from the root to the taxid, without "root" and "cellular organisms", separated by "; "), lineage_taxids (their taxids, in the same order, for an exact lowest common ancestor) and merged_into (the current taxid when the NCBI merged the taxid into another one; then the taxonomy is that of the current taxid; needs a database with the table merged, as built by make_taxonomy_db()).

See also

Other taxonomy functions: get_tax_online, make_taxonomy_db()

Examples

# a simplified NCBI taxdump: Hominidae with the genera Homo and Pan
taxdump <- file.path(tempdir(), "taxdump")
dir.create(taxdump, showWarnings = FALSE)
dmp <- function(...) paste0(paste(..., sep = "\t|\t"), "\t|")
writeLines(c(
  dmp(1, 1, "no rank"), dmp(2759, 1, "superkingdom"), dmp(9604, 2759, "family"),
  dmp(9605, 9604, "genus"), dmp(9606, 9605, "species"),
  dmp(9596, 9604, "genus"), dmp(9598, 9596, "species")
), file.path(taxdump, "nodes.dmp"))
writeLines(c(
  dmp(1, "root", "", "scientific name"), dmp(2759, "Eukaryota", "", "scientific name"),
  dmp(9604, "Hominidae", "", "scientific name"), dmp(9605, "Homo", "", "scientific name"),
  dmp(9606, "Homo sapiens", "", "scientific name"), dmp(9596, "Pan", "", "scientific name"),
  dmp(9598, "Pan troglodytes", "", "scientific name")
), file.path(taxdump, "names.dmp"))
tax_db <- make_taxonomy_db(tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite"), taxdump = taxdump)
#> ✔ Taxonomy database: /tmp/RtmpWKof0T/file19b74ca37d9a.sqlite (7 taxa).

# 1234 is not in this taxonomy: found = FALSE, with a warning
get_tax(c("9606", "9598", "1234"), taxonomy_db = tax_db)
#> Warning: ! 1 taxid not found in the taxonomy database: 1234
#> ℹ Use a taxonomy database as recent as the BLAST database (see
#>   `make_taxonomy_db()`).
#> # A tibble: 3 × 19
#>   taxid found sci_name      rank  domain kingdom phylum subphylum class subclass
#>   <chr> <lgl> <chr>         <chr> <chr>  <chr>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr>   
#> 1 9606  TRUE  Homo sapiens  spec… Eukar… NA      NA     NA        NA    NA      
#> 2 9598  TRUE  Pan troglody… spec… Eukar… NA      NA     NA        NA    NA      
#> 3 1234  FALSE NA            NA    NA     NA      NA     NA        NA    NA      
#> # ℹ 9 more variables: order <chr>, suborder <chr>, family <chr>,
#> #   subfamily <chr>, genus <chr>, species <chr>, lineage <chr>,
#> #   lineage_taxids <chr>, merged_into <chr>

# hits of two sequences: the first one tied between Homo and Pan
wide <- data.frame(
  Sequence = c("ACGT", "TTGA"),
  `1_subject` = c("A1", "B1"), `1_identity` = c(100, 99), `1_qcovhsp` = 100,
  `1_staxid` = "9606",
  `2_subject` = c("A2", "B2"), `2_identity` = c(99.8, 90), `2_qcovhsp` = 100,
  `2_staxid` = "9598",
  check.names = FALSE
)
hits <- as_blast_long(wide)
tax <- get_tax(hits, taxonomy_db = tax_db)
dplyr::left_join(hits, tax, by = c(staxid = "taxid"))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 43
#>   Sequence rank.x tie   at_best low_qcov informative uninformative_category
#>   <chr>     <int> <lgl> <lgl>   <lgl>    <lgl>       <chr>                 
#> 1 ACGT          1 FALSE TRUE    FALSE    NA          NA                    
#> 2 ACGT          2 FALSE TRUE    FALSE    NA          NA                    
#> 3 TTGA          1 FALSE TRUE    FALSE    NA          NA                    
#> 4 TTGA          2 FALSE FALSE   FALSE    NA          NA                    
#> # ℹ 36 more variables: blast_rank <int>, subject <chr>, `subject header` <chr>,
#> #   staxid <chr>, identity <dbl>, `Similarity score` <dbl>, qcovhsp <dbl>,
#> #   nident <dbl>, length <dbl>, mismatches <dbl>, gaps <dbl>,
#> #   `query start` <dbl>, `query end` <dbl>, `subject start` <dbl>,
#> #   `subject end` <dbl>, `subject strand` <chr>, `e-value` <dbl>,
#> #   bitscore <dbl>, found <lgl>, sci_name <chr>, rank.y <chr>, domain <chr>,
#> #   kingdom <chr>, phylum <chr>, subphylum <chr>, class <chr>, …
